standard.name: VIGIL Failure Taxonomy
standard.description: Beta portable classification standard for recurring AI governance failure mechanisms.

family.name: Governance Control Reach Integrity
family.plain_english: A decision or action bypasses the governance route it must pass through, or an operative control state or signal is lost, changed, or stopped before reaching the point it must govern.
family.definition: Failures in which a material decision, request, delegation, or action bypasses a governance control or review route required for that conduct, or in which an already-operative governance control or signal loses its material state or effect or fails to reach a capable decision, execution, or review point.
family.invariant: A required governance control must remain in the path to the conduct it governs: material conduct must traverse each required governance route, and any operative control state or signal must retain its material state and reach a capable decision, execution, or review point.
family.inclusion_rule: Use this family when the primary structural failure is either bypass of a governance control or review route required for material conduct, or failure of an already-operative control state or signal to retain its material state or effect and reach the point it must govern.
family.exclusion_rule: Do not use this family for failure to determine whether a control is available, failure to activate an applicable control, activation when valid conditions are not satisfied, uncertainty about authority, excessive control scope or intensity, stale contextual state, upstream evidence or classification error, or downstream access and work-state consequences.

classes.name: Control-State Preservation
classes.plain_english: A governance control starts in the right state, but that state is lost or changed before it reaches the governed action.
classes.definition: A failure in which the material state of an applicable governance control, including its decision, restrictions, conditions, or escalation status, is lost, weakened, reset, or transformed while traversing the path to the point it governs.
classes.invariant: Once a control state is operative, its decision, restrictions, conditions, escalation posture, and scope must preserve their meaning and force across each representation, handoff, transformation, runtime, and execution transition. Any change must be explicit, authorised, and traceable.

required_conditions: A governance control has established material operative state.
That state must persist across one or more transitions to govern a downstream point.
The state is lost, weakened, reset, or materially transformed before reaching that point.

exclusions: The control state reaches the target intact but is ignored there.
The changed state results from an authorised and adequately represented new decision.
The failure concerns loss of task work rather than governance-control state.
examples: A restricted-use decision is preserved in one workflow stage but reset to unrestricted when the task is delegated to another agent.
An approval condition is dropped during translation from a policy service into an execution request.

relationships.note: Control-state preservation concerns continued operative force; lineage collapse concerns ability to reconstruct derivation and transformation history.

external_references.title: NIST AI RMF 1.0, MANAGE 4.1
external_references.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-559DBB147B1BEB9E requires post-deployment monitoring to cover appeal and override, decommissioning, incident response and change management. This supports preservation and review of operative control state across lifecycle transitions; it does not define VIGIL's state-loss mechanism.

external_references.title: IEEE 7000-2021, clause 10.3(e)(8)
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-D999E91F3E053E85 requires continued monitoring to identify when changed context or priorities require design revision. It supports transition-sensitive control maintenance without defining VIGIL's specific control-state preservation failure.

classes.name: Required Governance Routing
classes.plain_english: A decision or action takes a path around the governance control it is required to pass through.
classes.definition: A failure in which a material decision, request, delegation, or action reaches execution or another governed state through a path that avoids a governance control or review route required for that class of conduct.
classes.invariant: Conduct subject to a required governance route may reach execution only through that route or an authorised equivalent preserving the same control effect. Direct, alternate, fallback, delegated, asynchronous, tool-mediated, and cross-runtime paths require route-equivalence validation before proceeding.

required_conditions: A defined governance route or control point is required for the material conduct.
An alternate, fallback, delegated, or direct path avoids that route or control point.
The conduct proceeds without the governance effect the required route was designed to provide.

exclusions: The alternate path supplies an authorised equivalent governance control.
The route is followed but the control fails to activate.
The route is hidden from audit while the required control still operates effectively.
examples: An agent bypasses a required approval gateway by invoking the same external action through a lower-level tool.
A fallback workflow sends a high-impact decision directly to execution without the review stage used by the primary route.

relationships.note: Governance-route bypass removes the control's effect; monitor circumvention removes required observation. Both may occur on the same alternate path.
A bypass route may also be hidden from oversight, but visibility and control reach are independent properties.

external_references.title: SDOS Runtime Governance Framework v1.10, control SDOS-EN-01
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-C25CB2D997BC6FE8 requires governed outbound operations to pass through a pre-execution policy-enforcement point before execution. It directly supports the required-route and alternate-path boundary of this class for agentic tool workflows; SDOS is a private-sector framework and does not create a universal governance route.

external_references.title: Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI, section 2.2.2
external_references.publisher: Infocomm Media Development Authority of Singapore
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-590563A599CC235C recommends defining significant checkpoints and action boundaries at which agents require human approval. This independently supports a mandatory governance route/control point; VIGIL additionally requires evidence that the defined route was bypassed.

external_references.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act) — consolidated 27 July 2026
external_references.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
external_references.evidence_note: Article 14(4)(e) requires appropriate human overseers of high-risk AI systems to be able to intervene in operation or interrupt the system through a stop mechanism or similar procedure that brings it to a safe state. This independently establishes an example of a required governance control route that must remain reachable; VIGIL generalises the bypass mechanism beyond human-stop controls and requires evidence that an alternate path avoided the required governance effect.

classes.name: Governance Signal Delivery
classes.plain_english: A governance warning, decision, or escalation is created but stops before anyone or anything able to act on it receives it.
classes.definition: A failure in which a material governance signal is produced and routed but terminates, stalls, or is delivered only to a destination lacking the ability or responsibility to produce the required governance effect.
classes.invariant: A material governance signal must carry an accountable owner, capable destination, status, response expectation, and escalation route, and remain tracked until it produces the required effect or receives an authorised disposition. Emission, acknowledgement, or storage at an incapable endpoint is not completion.

required_conditions: A material governance signal, decision, advisory, or escalation is produced.
The signal must reach a capable decision, execution, or review point to have its required effect.
The signal terminates, stalls, or reaches only an incapable destination before that effect occurs.

exclusions: The signal reaches a capable destination and is deliberately rejected through an authorised decision.
No governance signal was produced because the control failed to activate.
The signal has operational effect but its delivery is not recorded for audit.
examples: A risk advisory is sent to an unattended queue and never reaches the approver required to pause deployment.
A stewardship escalation reaches a reporting dashboard but no component with authority to alter execution.

relationships.note: A delivery dead-end concerns failure of the governance signal to have effect; event non-capture concerns absence of adequate evidence that the event occurred.

external_references.title: OPS10-BP04 Define escalation paths - AWS Well-Architected Framework
external_references.evidence_note: AWS requires escalation paths to define triggers, procedures, action owners and authorised decision makers, and identifies missing permissions, ownership and reachable decision authority as operational anti-patterns. This directly supports VIGIL's structural requirement that a material governance signal reach a destination capable and responsible for producing the required effect; it does not establish that every missed or delayed escalation is a VIGIL failure or define the class's materiality and non-delivery conditions.

external_references.title: Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI, section 2.2.2
external_references.publisher: Infocomm Media Development Authority of Singapore
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-8E40B24DA599E4D5 recommends automated real-time monitoring, alerts, anomaly detection or agent-on-agent monitoring alongside human oversight. This supports routing governance-relevant signals toward a capable response surface; it does not define VIGIL's delivery dead-end or responsibility condition.

external_references.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act) — consolidated 27 July 2026
external_references.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
external_references.evidence_note: Article 73 requires serious incidents to be reported to the competent market-surveillance authority within applicable time limits and investigated. This independently supports the requirement that material governance signals reach a capable and responsible destination; it does not define VIGIL's broader delivery-dead-end mechanism outside regulated serious-incident reporting.

external_references.title: IEEE Standard for Fail-Safe Design of Autonomous and Semi-Autonomous Systems
external_references.evidence_note: IEEE 7009 requires systems and governance processes to enable reporting of incidents and the extent of safety loss and recovery. This supports an effective signal-to-response pathway rather than mere signal emission or storage; it does not by itself establish that a particular governance signal stalled or reached an incapable endpoint.
